properties.plan_source: BCB 1905, fig. 166; round-2 drawing (Sep 30, 2026), outer face of the walls on the imagery
properties.description: house of 20 by 50 m formed by joining two blocks of the grid across a suppressed street, with a peristyle, a blue granite basin with pink marble columns, an oecus with the acanthus-hearts mosaic and baths on the east side (Ballu 1897b: 228-230; BCB 1905: 333-334; Germain 1969: 42-44)

properties.plan_source: Ballu II pp. 81-9; BCB pp. 326-33; Gsell f. 27; Courtois pp. 52-3; Germain p. 59

Ballu 1911a (Sept années): 74, plan of the house, with his description 72-73 (first published in his report on the 1906 excavations, Ballu 1907: 261-262); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the House of Corfidius Crementius, the fourth block of the third row of the north-west quarter, named from the inscription found in the atrium (1911a: 73-74); the outline follows the outer face of the outer walls, with the latrines projecting onto the cardo at the south-east corner, about 461 m²

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: outer face of the house's outer walls as drawn, about 2130 m² inside this line counting the cistern; Ballu gives 2,464 m², 200 m² more than the House of Sertius, the largest at Timgad until then, and Germain about 2,500 m², with some forty rooms round two courts (Ballu 1922: 47; 1923: 43, plan; Germain 1969: 81)

properties.plan_source: Traced from georeferenced satellite imagery; Ballu 1897: 224-226; BCB 1905: 88-92; Germain 1969: 37 and plan insula 70

properties.building_id: Grande maison au Nord du Capitole
properties.description: big house north of the Capitol cleared in 1916, with the small baths of 1915 at its north end and the two rooms cleared in 1925 between them, which Ballu then saw were one house with its own baths (Ballu 1916: 176-179; 1925: 35-36); about 98 m along the street and 20 m wide with the apsed hall at its south end, three entrances on the street, two of them behind porticoes, and a mosaic floor in most rooms, which led Germain to think it looked more like a building for a group than a private house (1969: 106, 118)

properties.plan_source: round-2 drawing (outer face of the walls)
properties.description: Large warehouse with a central court and storerooms, plus a small mosaic-paved residence and private baths. Germain's "Maison au sud de la porte de Lambèse"

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1909: 94-95 (BCTH; offprint pp. 22-23, the report on the 1908 excavations) and 1911a (Sept années): 67-68; Courtois 1951 city plan; round-2 drawing (Oct 6, 2026), outer face of the walls on the satellite imagery
properties.description: Ballu's fourth block of the north-west quarter, the first house of the second row from the north boulevard, on the west boulevard, which he called by far the finest and best preserved (*C'est de beaucoup le plus beau et le mieux conservé*, it is by far the finest and the best preserved, 1909: 94); entered from the north in its axis through a vestibule into a paved atrium with four porticoes and a square limestone basin, the tablinum south of the atrium, and an east fraction of smaller rooms on the north and east streets

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 229, fig. 11.5; Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; Ballu, BCTH 1912: 493-494; round-2 drawing (Oct 2, 2026), outer face of the walls on the imagery
properties.description: block house filling the seventh *îlot* Ballu cleared in 1911 in the north-east quarter, between the fourth and fifth Decumanus; he says the block held two dyers' workshops separated by an east-west wall, the north one with five rooms, two of them paved in stone and the one in the north-west corner with a well and two fulling vats, and besides those two large halls of equal size opening on the east and west streets, the south one with eight rooms, one large and one still holding a terracotta vat (Ballu, BCTH 1912: 493-494); it's Amraoui's *insula* 20, with a small *fullonica* in the north-west corner (Amraoui 2020b: 228-229, fig. 11.5)

properties.plan_source: Germain 1969, fig. 7; Ballu 1903, pl. XXIII (east annex)
properties.description: round-2 outline, extended east to the corridor room and apse that all three plans draw beyond the round-1 polygon

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 234, fig. 11.9; Christofle's plan in Wilson 2001: 275, fig. 12.04; Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; Ballu, BCTH 1912: 494; round-2 drawing (Sep 29, 2026), outer face of the walls on the imagery
properties.description: block of the ninth house Ballu cleared in 1911 in the north-east quarter, west of the seventh, between the fourth and fifth Decumanus; he says a north-south wall split it into two like halves, two more fullers' establishments, the west one with ten rooms, four of them paved in stone, two with wells, a passage and a room with a basin, and the east one with two rooms on the north street filled by a well, two basins and three fulling tubs, and seven other rooms (Ballu, BCTH 1912: 494); it's Amraoui's *insula* 19, with the *fullonica* in rooms 9 and 10 in the north-east corner, part of a unit of four rooms, two more units of a *taberna* and a back room south of it, and a house in the other half whose owner, she says, must have rented the three units out (Amraoui 2020b: 233-234, fig. 11.9), though her text has east and west the other way round from her plan

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020a: 134, fig. 4.11; Amraoui 2020b: 235, fig. 11.10; Christofle's plan in Wilson 2001: 274, fig. 12.01; Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), outer face of the walls on the imagery
properties.description: block of Amraoui's *insula* 30 in the north-east quarter, whose north-east quarter is the largest fulling workshop in Timgad, rooms 8, 9 and 10 with their eleven compartments and the well, while the rest, she says, holds two shops and a house (Amraoui 2020a: 134-135, fig. 4.11; 2020b: 234-235, fig. 11.10); the fullery has its own three street openings on the north, one into room 8 and two into room 9, and no door into the rest of the block, room 1 and room 2 with room 4 behind it each open on a street on their own, and the rest, room 3 with its well, rooms 5, 6 and 7 and, through the middle wall, rooms 11 to 14, hang together from the street door of room 5 on the west; the block was dug between 1908 and 1913 (Wilson 2001: 273) and Ballu's notice of it should be in the report Wilson cites (Ballu 1911a: 123-126), which isn't in the folder, and Christofle's plan of the fullery (Wilson 2001: 274, fig. 12.01, after Christoflé 1935: 77) is the second witness for the north-east corner; the block as a whole is probable, its outline certain on every plan and the ground, its inside from Amraoui's plan

properties.plan_source: Meunier's unpublished 1938 plan of the house, the fragment Germain reproduces (Germain 1969: 122, fig. 17, right), read from Rebuffat's larger reproduction of it (Rebuffat 1974: pl. 'Thamugadi 12'), with Germain's notes on the floors (1969: 125-127, nos 190-192) and Ballu's plan of the complex (Ballu 1911a: 33) for comparison; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the House of Optat, inside the Donatist episcopal quarter west of the Capitol, in the space between the cathedral's east wall and the chapel (Germain 1969: 122); a peristyle house with its mosaic portico and the inscription room on the west, the hall north of the court and the south portico along the south side; the outline follows the outer face of its walls, with the cathedral's wall as its west side, about 588 m²; no excavation-era plan or description was published, the plan is Meunier's of 1938 as Germain gives it

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; Ballu, BCTH 1912: 494-495; round-2 drawing (Oct 5, 2026), outer face of the walls on the satellite imagery
properties.description: house filling the whole block, the tenth and last *insula* (city block) Ballu cleared in 1911 in the north-east quarter, north of the ninth, between the fifth *decumanus* (east-west street) and the north boulevard; he says it was used by two dyers (*deux industriels en teinturerie*) and split by a median wall, with four shops along the west and south streets in the west half

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; Ballu, BCTH 1912: 493; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), outer face of the walls on the satellite imagery
properties.description: house filling the whole block, the fifth private building (*construction particulière*) Ballu cleared in 1911 in the north-east quarter, between the fourth and fifth *decumanus* (east-west streets), north of the fourth house; he says a party wall split it into two equal halves, and takes it there were two dyers in the house

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31); round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026), outer face of the walls on the satellite imagery
properties.description: house filling the whole block, the sixth building (*immeuble*) Ballu cleared in 1911 in the north-east quarter, between the fifth *decumanus* (east-west street) on the south and the city's north boulevard, north of the fifth house (NE.I29); he says two craftsmen lived here (*là aussi logeaient deux industriels*, here too lived two craftsmen), divided by a north-south wall, each with a long room or two, a room along the *decumanus* and, in the east half, three rooms on the east street

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32); round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026), outer face of the walls on the satellite imagery
properties.description: house filling the whole block, the eighth building Ballu cleared in 1911 in the north-east quarter, north of the seventh (NE.I28) and running up to the north boulevard like the sixth, with the fifth *decumanus* (east-west street) on its south; he calls it carefully built and worth a special mention (*de structure soignée et mérite une mention spéciale*), divided into two equal halves by a north-south wall, one half with a fine stone-paved atrium with a big well, a semicircular wall behind it and three basins in front, a corner room with a well and a fulling vat and seven more rooms, the other with two rooms with wells and vats, a fairly large hall and four other rooms (Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32)); on the ground the atrium's well and curved wall are in the west half, where he puts them in the east
